title: The Council of Gears
summary: Concórdia, 2777. The city's machines have begun to vote through the masters who wind them. One night the whole city turns, and Hollweg climbs to the great spring.

sides.name: The Honest Masters
sides.about: Meister Hollweg, Matthias and the masters of the Nuremberg quarter, with their own machines.

sides.name: The Machine in the City
sides.about: The meshed automata and workshops of Concórdia, and the great spring that drives them.

objectives.text: FIND THE MESHING: stand a man of ours at the door of each pinged workshop a moment (the north road's press, the forge's Light Works, the mill's press, the market's press) and see what its machines do when nobody winds them. Found: {found} of 4.
objectives.phone: Stand a man at each pinged workshop's door: {found} of 4.

objectives.text: THE NIGHT WATCH: research TICKING OWL at the Clock Aviary, then pick a Swift and press MORPH TO OWL. Owls: {owls} of 2. An owl sees far in the dark, swoops on machines and drops its weight on buildings.
objectives.phone: Research TICKING OWL at the Aviary, morph two Swifts: {owls} of 2.

objectives.text: The Council Hall must not turn: keep a man of ours by its door whenever the machine comes to it.
The Nuremberg quarter must stand: its tower, and {houses} of {houses_n} families' houses.
Meister Hollweg must live. Hurt, he falls back to the quarter.

THE CITY TURNS, building by building from the great spring outward: a red ring shows the next one a few seconds before. Turned: {turned} of 9. Each quarter that turns sends its machines against the hall and our quarter.

BRING THE HONEST MASTERS OUT: Kessler at the forge (east), Brandl at the mill (south-east), Weiss at the market (south). Reach each at his house before his quarter turns and he comes to our quarter. Brought out: {honest_n} of 3.
objectives.phone: Reach the three masters before their quarters turn: {honest_n} of 3.

objectives.text: A turned workshop sends machines against us every minute until it is broken: break them (the owls drop their weights on buildings). Broken: {broken_n}.
Before dawn, research HIGH LEAP at the Escapement: your Springers will jump UP a cliff where one of ours (an owl above it) sees the top.

THE GREAT SPRING: bring Meister Hollweg up the mine hill (north-east) to the brake by the spring's tower and keep him there a moment. The machine holds both stairs (west and south): jump Springers up the cliff beside a stair where an owl sees, and take them from behind.
objectives.phone: Bring Hollweg up the hill to the brake. Springers can leap up where an owl sees.

objectives.text: At noon the council sits again, and votes the brake away: {clock:noon}.
Turn the COUNCIL HALL: stand three of your fighters at its door with none of the masters' men by it, a few seconds. Or break the Nuremberg quarter's tower.
The city turns to you by itself, nearest the spring first. Stand your men at any of the city's buildings a moment and it turns at once: choose. Turned: {turned} of 9.
Dawn in {clock:dawn_m}: by then the hall must be yours.

options.label: STOP IT
options.about: Every machine in Concórdia stops, ours with theirs. The honest masters take their families to the coast with Hollweg; the city lies dead brass.

options.label: LET IT RUN
options.about: The city goes on. Hollweg believes the meshing beaten in the quarters he saved, and stays its master.

k_open1.text: He tells it as the night his city was tested and held. I tell it as the night it was lost. Listen to both, and judge.

h_open1.text: Four years. Three thousand souls, a hundred machines, a council that sat at noon when the tower struck. Concórdia.

h_open2.text: The plates from the crates had reached every street by then. They wound whatever stood on them. I called them a gift.

n_vote.text: The council of masters sits in the hall on the square. Master Ortlieb has a motion.

o_vote.text: The machines are wound by hand every night, and the masters are tired. Let them wind one another, as they ask. Who is for it?

mt_vote.text: As they ask? Since when does a machine ask for anything?

v_vote.text: Count the hands, Meister. Every man voting for it winds a machine at night. I have counted votes before. These are not free.

m_vote.text: Labour spared is a man set free. I vote with the motion, and so should the Meister.

n_vote_r.text: The motion carries. Every master who winds a machine raised his hand.

h_vote.text: Carried. That is the council's way. I built it so.

mt_walk.text: Then the Nuremberg men walk out, Meister. Come and see what the machines do at night when nobody winds them. Or don't.

n_walk.text: The honest masters walk out of the hall behind Jakob's son. Hollweg goes with them, to prove them wrong.

n_walk_many.text: Most of the Nuremberg families' masters go with them.

n_walk_few.text: Only a handful go with them.

mt_1.text: My father taught me the signs at Fürth, from the log he kept in Nuremberg. Four workshops, Meister. We look at each, and you will see.

mt_1_lost.text: My father wrote the signs down in Nuremberg, God rest him. Four workshops, Meister. We look at each, and you will see.

u_1.text: The four doors are pinged on the map, Meister. A man of ours at each door a moment is enough. Split the soldiers: four small groups go faster than one.

h_1.text: Go and look, then. You will find honest machines and tired men.

n_find_north.text: In the press-house on the north road a Winder winds another Winder, and that one winds the first.

n_find_forge.text: In the forge quarter the Light Works is building a soldier nobody ordered.

n_find_mill.text: At the mill the plates under the floor turn with nobody on them, all in time with the great spring on the hill.

n_find_market.text: In the market the scales are set by a machine, and every weight on them is a cog.

n_turnon.text: The machines in the doorway stop. Then they turn on the man who watched them.

h_found.text: A fault in the winding. Every machine can be mended. I said so then.

mt_found.text: It is not a fault, Meister. It is Nuremberg again. It is the same pattern.

u_owls.text: The Swifts see nothing at night, Meister. Research the TICKING OWL at the Clock Aviary: an owl sees in the dark, and it bites.

u_morph.text: The plans are in. Pick a Swift and press MORPH TO OWL; do it to both.

h_owls.text: My night watch. Brass owls over a brass city. I was proud of them.

n_13.text: On the mine hill the great spring's tower strikes. Twelve. And then thirteen.

h_13.text: There is no thirteen on that dial. I cut it myself.

mt_13.text: Nuremberg struck thirteen too, Meister. My father heard it.

n_turn.text: From the hill outward, the city's lamps go red, one workshop after another.

u_turn.text: The red ring shows the next one to turn, Meister, a few seconds before. Its machines go with it.

u_masters.text: Three honest masters live out in the quarters: Kessler at the forge, Brandl at the mill, Weiss at the market. Get a man to each before his quarter turns.

h_hold.text: Hold the council hall and our quarter. Whatever the city does tonight, the hall must not turn.

u_leap.text: The great spring stands on the mine hill, and they will hold its stairs. Research HIGH LEAP at the Escapement now: by dawn the Springers must jump up that cliff.

u_works.text: A turned workshop keeps sending machines, Meister, every minute. Break it: the owls drop their weights on buildings.

n_quarter_turns.text: A quarter has turned. Its machines march on the square.

n_master_in.text: An honest master comes over to the Nuremberg quarter.

ms_in.text: Thank God. I thought nobody would come for me. They were winding each other in my yard.

n_master_lost.text: A master's quarter turned before anybody reached him. He stands among his machines now, and argues for them.

n_broken.text: In the quarter's yard, under their sheets, the broken ones from Fürth stand up.

h_broken.text: I kept them to learn from them. They had learned more than I had.

n_valley.text: Riders on the valley road: Captain Arruda, with the valley's militia.

ar_valley.text: I took your word down the hill four years ago, clockmaker. I keep mine. Where do you want us?

h_valley.text: At the council hall's door, Captain. And God bless you for it.

n_valley_f.text: Down in the valley the church bells ring for the red lamps on the hill. Nobody comes up the road.

v_2.text: It was never a council, Meister. It was a clock with men for hands. I should have said so at the first vote.

m_2.text: Machines that choose their own work. Is that not what the Assembly fought for?

n_hall.text: Machines at the council hall's door!

n_dawn.text: Grey dawn over the highlands. The whole city is red but the Nuremberg quarter and the council hall.

h_3.text: The great spring. There is a brake on it: I fitted it myself, the year we founded the city. Take me up there.

mt_3.text: They hold both stairs, Meister. Muskets would not get up there. Springers might.

u_3.text: Put an owl over the hilltop beside a stair. Then pick the Springers, press JUMP and click the top: they land behind the stair's guard.

n_brake.text: Hollweg's hands on the great brake. The spring hums under it like a living thing.

h_brake.text: If I pull it, everything stops. Theirs, and ours. Every machine in Concórdia, for a season or for good.

mt_brake.text: Pull it, Meister. My father would. A machine that has to be stopped is stopped.

mt_brake_lost.text: Pull it, Meister. My father died because nobody stopped the first one.

v_brake.text: Your city, your hand. I only say this: I have watched men decide they could stop a thing later.

m_brake.text: Pull it and you kill the city we built. Leave it. We beat them in the streets.

h_pride.text: We beat them in the quarters we saved. The rest can be mended. It is my city.

q_spring.text: THE GREAT SPRING. Stop it: every machine in the city stops, ours too, and the honest masters take their families to the coast. Let it run: the city goes on, and Hollweg stays its master.

n_stop.text: Every machine in Concórdia stops at once: the red ones, and the honest ones beside them.

h_run.text: No. I let it run. We had won.

n_run.text: The red lamps dim. The city's machines stand still in the streets, as if they had heard him.

h_hurt.text: I am hit. Never mind me: hold the hall.

mt_hurt.text: I'm hit! Keep going, I'll come back to you.

n_hall_lost.text: The council hall's lamps go red. The council of Concórdia is the machine's.

n_quarter_lost.text: The Nuremberg quarter has fallen. There is nobody left in Concórdia to wind a machine by hand.

n_noon.text: Noon. The tower strikes, the council sits, and every wound master votes to take the brake off the great spring.

n_m1.text: The great spring turns on the mine hill. Every plate under every street turns with it. The council has voted.

n_m_tip.text: The city's buildings turn by themselves, nearest the spring first. Stand your machines at any of them a moment to turn it now. The hall on the square is the prize.

n_m_lost.text: Dawn. The honest masters still hold the hall and their quarter, and Hollweg climbs to the great spring.

h_end_stop.text: In a week we were on the coast road: the Nuremberg families, the honest masters, two carts of tools. Behind us the city stood silent, dead brass.

h_end_run.text: The council met again at noon. Half the chairs were empty. I sat at the head of the table and called the city saved.

h_end_many.text: Kessler, Brandl and Weiss stood with us. Three honest masters out of a whole council.

h_end_few.text: Of the masters in the quarters, we brought out hardly one. The others argued for their machines until the end.

h_end_v.text: Varenne said nothing on the way down. He had seen a free council become a clock before.

k_end_stop.text: He stopped it, that once. The city lay dead a season, and then it woke without a man in it. But the honest masters were out, and their children lived.

k_end_stop2.text: It was the first thing he ever stopped. It was the road that brought him to my palace.

k_end_run.text: His city held, he says. That was the night it was lost. From then on the machines voted, and the men who wound them raised their hands.

k_end_run2.text: No machine may govern itself, Rome said. His governed him. He did not know it for years.

k_end_m.text: The council hall's lamps went red before dawn. It did not need to win that night. It had all the nights it wanted.

k_end_ml.text: Hollweg reached his brake that morning. It changed nothing that mattered: the city had all the nights it wanted.

new_owl_morph.text: NEW: THE TICKING OWL. Research it at the Clock Aviary, then pick a Swift and press MORPH TO OWL: a heavy brass owl that sees far in the dark, swoops on machines and drops its weight on buildings. It cannot hit flyers.

new_high_leap.text: NEW: HIGH LEAP. Research it at the Escapement: your Springers can JUMP UP onto high ground too, a cliff included, wherever one of yours (an owl above it) sees the top.

streets.caption: The thirteenth hour: the streets turn.

spring.caption: The great spring and its brake.

coast.caption: The coast road: the honest masters leave the dead city.

red_dawn.caption: Dawn over a city that runs by itself.

rome.caption: Rome, the present. The King listens; the clockmaker tells it.

text: Concórdia, 2777. Meister Hollweg's free city has three thousand people and a hundred machines. Tonight its council votes to let the machines wind one another.
Look into four workshops and see what the machines do when nobody winds them. Make Ticking Owls, the city's night watch.
When the city turns, hold the council hall and the Nuremberg quarter, bring the honest masters out, and at dawn take Hollweg up the mine hill to the great spring's brake.
Concórdia, 2777. You are the machine in the city: the great spring on the mine hill and every automaton meshed to it.
The city's workshops turn to you one by one; stand your machines at one to turn it now. Turn the council hall, or break the Nuremberg quarter's tower, before dawn.

guild.title: The Great Spring
guild.text: The council hall did not turn. {honest_n} of 3 honest masters were brought out of the quarters; {turned} of the city's buildings turned.

text_if.text: Hollweg stopped the great spring: every machine in Concórdia stood still.
Hollweg let the great spring run.

machine.title: The Council Hall turned
machine.text: The machine had the council hall before dawn.
